h1: The 8 Best Server Racks for Small Offices and Home Labs, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Server Racks for Office: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 server racks for offices from 18U wall mounts to 42U cabinets, compared on depth, weight rating, cooling, doors and mobility.
summary: The Sysracks 42U 32 inch cabinet on wheels is the best server rack for most offices, with a 1600 pound static rating, roof fans, an 8-way PDU and a perforated front door. The StarTech 22U cabinet suits small rooms, the 18U wall-mount rack saves floor space, and the StarTech 42U open frame suits adjustable depth.
intro: Most people buy a rack by height and then discover the depth was the problem. A 42U cabinet sounds generous until your server turns out to be 30 inches deep with cables, and the door will not close. Depth, not height, decides which gear fits, and the rack's usable depth is always shorter than its outer size.

We ranked eight racks, from an 18U wall mount to full 42U cabinets, by weight rating, depth, cooling, door design and whether they roll. We note that the weight ratings are static: they apply when the rack stands still, not while you move it loaded. Where listings leave out a figure, we say so.

products.name: Sysracks 42U Server Rack Cabinet, 32in Deep, on Wheels
products.verdict: A 42U, 32 inch deep cabinet with a 1600 pound static rating, roof fans and an 8-way PDU.
products.description:
The Sysracks cabinet is 42U tall and 32 inches deep, rated for 1600 pounds static, with four roof-mounted fans, an 8-way PDU, a perforated glass front door and a solid metal rear door, mounted on wheels. It costs $500 and up.

It wins because it is complete: cooling, power distribution and lockable doors in one purchase. The perforated front lets air in while the glass shows status lights, and roof fans pull hot air up. A 32 inch depth fits most office gear, though not the deepest servers.

Buy it for a full office server closet. Measure the deepest device first.
products.idealFor: Offices with a closet for full-size gear.

products.name: 42U Home Server Rack Cabinet, 35in Deep Homelab Rack
products.verdict: A 35 inch deep 42U cabinet with fans, PDU, shelf, casters and leveling feet included.
products.description:
This homelab rack is 42U tall and 35 inches deep with a 1600 pound static rating, integrated cooling fans and ventilation, and includes a PDU, shelf, casters and leveling feet. It costs $500 and up.

Three extra inches of depth over the Sysracks 32 inch let it take longer servers and leave cable room behind. The included accessories save money. It sits second because the listing is thinner on door design.

Buy it for a home lab with deep gear. Check door details before ordering.

products.name: Sysracks 42U Server Rack Cabinet, 39in Deep, Floor Standing
products.verdict: A 39 inch deep 42U cabinet with LCD temperature control, four fans, a PDU and a shelf.
products.description:
The 39 inch Sysracks cabinet is 42U tall with LCD temperature control, four built-in fans, a PDU and a fixed shelf. It is floor standing and costs $500 and up.

It is the choice for the deepest gear, and the LCD temperature control tells you how hot the cabinet is. It ranks third because it is fixed in place, with no wheels, and the listing gives no weight rating.

Buy it for deep servers in a permanent spot. Check the weight rating.
products.idealFor: Deep servers in a permanent spot.
products.skipIf: You need to move the cabinet.

products.name: StarTech 22U 4-Post Server Cabinet, 33in Deep, 1764lb
products.verdict: A 22U, 33 inch deep cabinet rated for 1764 pounds, 46.6 inches tall, with wheels.
products.description:
The StarTech 22U cabinet is 33 inches deep and 46.6 inches tall, with a 1764 pound stationary rating and included wheels and leveling feet. It costs $500 and up.

It is a heavy-duty cabinet that fits under a desk or in a small room. The high static rating exceeds most larger cabinets. It ranks fourth because 22U limits expansion.

Buy it for a small room with heavy gear. Choose 42U for growth.

products.name: StarTech 42U 4-Post Open Frame Rack, 22-40in Adjustable Depth
products.verdict: A 42U open frame with 22 to 40 inch adjustable depth and a 1323 pound rating.
products.description:
This open frame rack is 42U with an adjustable depth of 22 to 40 inches, a 1323 pound static rating, EIA/ECA-310-E compliance and cage nuts included. It costs $200 to $500.

An open frame has no doors, so it breathes freely and costs less. Adjustable depth fits shallow and deep gear. It ranks fifth because it offers no lock and no dust protection.

Buy it for a locked room or a noisy-free server closet. Skip it where security matters.

products.name: StarTech 24U 4-Post Server Cabinet, 29in Deep, 992lb
products.verdict: A 24U, 48.9 inch tall cabinet with 29 inch adjustable depth and a 5-year warranty.
products.description:
The StarTech 24U cabinet is 48.9 inches tall with a 29 inch adjustable depth, a 992 pound stationary capacity, a 5-year warranty and a 1U fixed shelf. It costs $500 and up.

The five-year warranty is rare in this category. It ranks sixth because the rating is lower and 29 inches is shallow for deep servers.

Buy it for a small, shallow-gear office. Choose a deeper cabinet for servers.

products.name: NavePoint 22U Server Cabinet Wall Mount Rack Enclosure
products.verdict: A 22U wall-mount enclosure with two fans and a lockable glass door, 130 pound capacity.
products.description:
The NavePoint is a 22U wall-mount enclosure measuring 23.63 by 23.63 by 43 inches, with a 130 pound capacity, two built-in fans and a lockable glass door. It costs $200 to $500.

Wall mounting frees floor space, but 130 pounds is a low limit, so it suits switches and patch panels, not servers. It ranks seventh for that reason.

Buy it for network gear on a wall. Do not load it with servers.

products.name: 18U Wall Mount Server Rack Cabinet, 24-Inch Deep
products.verdict: An 18U wall mount with 20 inch usable depth, a top fan, two shelves and a PDU.
products.description:
This wall-mount cabinet is 18U with 24 inches overall and 20 inches usable depth, a 133 pound capacity, a top fan, two shelves and a PDU. It costs $200 to $500.

It is the smallest of the group, and the included shelves and PDU add value. It ranks last because 20 inches of usable depth limits it to shallow network gear.

Buy it for a router, switch and modem closet. Not for servers.

methodology.description: Fans, perforated doors and open frames were weighed for airflow, and locks for security.

methodology.title: Mobility and extras
methodology.description: Wheels, leveling feet, PDUs and shelves were credited for ready-to-use value.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Price tiers of $200 to $500 and up were set against capacity and included parts.

whatMatters.detail: Measure your deepest device and add room for cables, usually three to four inches. A rack's usable depth is less than its outer depth. Choose the depth first.
One U is 1.75 inches of vertical space. A 42U rack has 42 slots. Plan for growth but remember taller racks need ceiling clearance.
Static ratings apply when the rack is not moving. Wall mounts carry far less. Add up equipment weight and stay below it.
Perforated doors, fans and open frames keep gear cool. A sealed cabinet traps heat. Check for fans and ventilation.
Lockable doors protect equipment, while open frames offer none. Fans add noise. Consider where the rack sits.

cards.label: Enclosed cabinet
cards.text: Doors protect and lock, and fans manage heat. The Sysracks and StarTech cabinets do this.

cards.label: Open frame
cards.text: No doors for easy access and airflow. The StarTech 42U Open Frame is the pick.

howToChoose.note: Choose enclosed for shared offices and open frame for locked rooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Quiet fans, a door that closes, a size that fits a closet and wheels to move it.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The StarTech 22U fits small rooms, and the Sysracks 42U on wheels suits a closet.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run servers and need cooling and doors. The Sysracks at $500 and up includes them.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only hold switches. A wall mount at $200 to $500 is enough.

faq.a: One rack unit is 1.75 inches of height. A 42U rack holds 42 of them. Check your devices' U sizes.
Ignoring depth. A tall rack that is too shallow will not close. Measure your deepest device.

faq.q: Is a cabinet worth it over open frame?
faq.a: For shared spaces, yes, because doors lock and filter dust. For a locked room, open frame costs less.

faq.q: How do I assemble a rack?
faq.a: Most arrive flat. Allow two people and a few hours. Level it and bolt it down if the manual advises.

faq.q: How do I cool a cabinet?
faq.a: Use fans, perforated doors and cable management. Do not block vents. Keep the room temperature moderate.

faq.q: Can a wall mount hold servers?
faq.a: Usually not. Capacities of 130 pounds suit switches. Use a floor rack for servers.

finalTake: The Sysracks 42U 32 inch on wheels is the best server rack for most offices because it includes cooling, a PDU and a solid rating. Pick the 35 inch homelab cabinet for deeper gear, the StarTech 22U for small rooms and the open frame for a locked closet. Always check depth first.
